title: Serenity (Firefly)
intro: Serenity is the fictional Firefly-class transport of Captain Malcolm Reynolds in the series Firefly and the film Serenity, flown by the pilot Wash. Its small bridge at the nose mixes a ship's bridge and an aircraft cockpit: the pilot's station on the left, a second station on the right, and room for the whole crew to gather.

areas.name: Forward windows
areas.text: The wide windows of the bridge.

panels.name: Forward windows
panels.text: The wide windows at the front of the bridge.
panels.context: They give the pilot the view for landing and for flying through danger.

controls.name: Bridge windows
controls.text: Wide windows give a broad view forward from Serenity's bridge.
controls.context: The pilot looks out through them when landing on planets.

areas.name: Pilot's console
areas.text: The crowded console at the pilot's station.

panels.name: Pilot's console
panels.text: A crowded console of screens and switches in front of the pilot.
panels.context: The pilot flies the ship and watches the systems from here.

controls.name: Screens
controls.text: Screens show the navigation and the sensors.
controls.context: They help the pilot find the way and see other ships.

controls.name: Switch rows
controls.text: Rows of switches for the engines and the ship's systems.
controls.context: The series shows the pilot working them; each switch is not explained.

controls.name: Toy dinosaurs
controls.text: Wash keeps toy dinosaurs on the console. They are decoration and do nothing for the ship.
controls.context: They show that the bridge is a lived-in place, part of the character of the series.

areas.name: Co-pilot's console
areas.text: The second station on the right.

panels.name: Co-pilot's console
panels.text: The second station on the right side of the bridge.
panels.context: Another crew member can sit and help here.

controls.name: Second station
controls.text: The second station is used by the captain or another crew member.
controls.context: It lets a second person watch the systems or talk on the radio while the pilot flies.

panels.name: Overhead switches
panels.text: Panels of switches above the pilot's head.
panels.context: They belong to the ship's systems.

controls.name: Overhead switches
controls.text: Switches for the ship's systems above the pilot's head.
controls.context: The pilot reaches up to them during flight; the series does not name each one.

areas.name: Yoke and thrust controls
areas.text: The hand controls the pilot flies with.

panels.name: Control yoke
panels.text: The control yoke at the pilot's station on the left.
panels.context: The pilot steers the ship with both hands.

controls.name: Control yoke
controls.text: Pushing the yoke forward or pulling it back tips the nose down or up; turning it rolls and banks the ship.
controls.context: It is held with both hands, like the yoke of an airliner.

panels.name: Thrust controls
panels.text: The thrust levers on the pilot's console.
panels.context: They set how hard the engines push.

controls.name: Thrust controls
controls.text: Levers on the console that set how hard the engines push.
controls.context: The catalog takes them as the engine thrust; the series does not show them in detail.
